In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
RNF43 and its paralogue ZNRF3 have a critical role in serrated colorectum tumourigenesis, and are likely to be therapeutic targets for this disease.

the serrated pathway of colorectal tumourigenesis is characterised by a mutation of the ubiquitylation ligases RNF4 and ZNRF4, which is associated with reduced expression of the ligases and increased Wnt signalling.
RNF43 and/or ZNRF3 inactivation occurs in 80% of serrated pathway cancers, and is associated with reduced protein expression and reduced sensitivity to a Wnt inhibitor.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
RNF43 and its close homolog ZNRF3 act as negative regulators of Wnt signalling and are commonly mutated in BRAF mutated colorectal cancers.
RNF43 is a key driver of serrated tumour growth and that targeting RNF43 may provide a therapeutic strategy for this aggressive cancer subtype.

the Wnt signalling pathway is commonly up-regulated in colorectal cancer through mutations in APC, but that in serrated cancers this up-regulation occurs via inactivation of the ubiquitin-ligases RNF43/ZNRF3, which normally degrade the Wnt signalling receptor Frizzled.
